checks: Checked original note 185fb6155f830e0e §4, (8)–(10), and matched its source JSON byte digest. Its geometric proof only needs the common-direction and exact-section assertions from the joint law. The source application had q<N, but the section and shear proof uses no rank bound.

Lattice completeness puts z_0 in P. For sufficiently small 0<t<1, the point (z_0−t times the average of P)/(1−t) stays in the base hull by relative interior. Adding back weight t spread evenly over P gives a representation of z_0 with positive weight on every site, including the singleton case.

Incidence rigidity gives one support tangent V. The entire placed support hull is compact and convex, projects onto the entire base hull, and has exactly the stated S_z at integer bases by the predecessor.

For any y in the relative interior of the hull with base p, (z_0−t p)/(1−t) is in the base hull for small positive t. Combining y with a hull point over that base places a scaled relative ball in the hull over z_0. Intersecting that relative ball with the vertical affine fiber proves that the direction of S_z0 is the full vertical kernel.

The perpendicular component annihilates the vertical kernel, so it factors uniquely as an affine map on aff(P) because projection is onto aff(P). This gives the perpendicular offset at every site, including q=0 and lower-dimensional base hulls.

On aff(P)×R^D the shear is an affine bijection with inverse adding b(z). Each base is fixed and each fiber map is an intrinsic translation, preserving its Euclidean q-volume, with counting measure when q=0. Invertibility gives the affine halfspace correspondence in that space.

overlap.comparison: Its full-support representation on a minimal face supplies the all-base incidence when the face is the entire base hull. It does not yield tangent rigidity or a common affine perpendicular offset for joint measures.

Gives exact hull sections for compatible families and affineness of representation-preserving functions on the canonical placement. The present vertical-kernel argument proves the physical support offset is affine on the original placement under the interior integer hypothesis.

Its shear uses an affine recentering after a canonical lift or on an already canonical base. It does not derive the original-base affine support planes from a joint measure inequality and an interior integer site.
